title: Cost Optimizer — Executive Digest and Implementation Sketch for Batching/Cache/Quantization
body:
Summary

This note captures a compact set of recommended defaults and an experiment plan for lowering inference unit cost across common customer archetypes by combining micro-batching, keyed-prefix caching, and staged quantization. The goal is pragmatic: reduce per-token cost by 20–40% on median workloads while keeping p95 tail latency deviation below +20ms and limiting quality regressions to detectable/easy-to-roll-back changes.

Background and motivation

We have many existing heuristics for batching, caching, and quantization, but customers and sales/solutions teams repeatedly ask for a small, actionable starting point they can use in hosted and Dedicated. Past playbooks are fragmented and use different terms; this digest translates operational knobs into a concise, testable config matrix and concrete spreadsheet metrics the field can run.

Archetypes targeted here

1) Session-heavy conversational apps (chat apps, product-support assistants)
   - Characteristic: long histories, repeated prefixes, sticky sessions, moderate RPS (1–50 req/s per deployment), high variance in sequence lengths.
2) Stateless short-completions (search snippets, single-turn prompts)
   - Characteristic: short inputs, high RPS (100–1,000 req/s), bounded output length, little prefix reuse.
3) Mixed bursty APIs (interactive assistants with occasional long generations)
   - Characteristic: low average RPS but high burstiness, variable sequences.

Key recommended defaults (initial config)

Note: these are intended as starting points for A/B testing; conservative defaults prioritize latency SLOs. Values are expressed as recommended API/runtime config keys.

- Global knobs
  - default_batch_window_ms: 10ms (captures short micro-batches across pipelined requests while minimizing tail impact)
  - max_batch_size: 64 for GPU-backed large models (Llama2-70B-class), 128 for smaller models (7B–13B)
  - session_kv_cache_enabled: true
  - session_kv_cache_ttl_seconds: 900 for sticky sessions; 300 for public-facing consumer bots
  - prefix_cache_enabled: true on routes with >15% prefix reuse measured in the last 24h

- Quantization staging (safety-first ordering)
  1) Run int8 dynamic per-layer emulation in inference-sim on 1% traffic (no quality gating) to gather perf signals.
  2) If average quality (eval set) drop <= 0.8% relative and p95 latency improves, promote to 10% traffic with automatic rollback if eval delta > 1.5%.
  3) For further cost reductions, test int4 (group-wise) with careful KL-based sample checks and only on low-risk routes (internal tools, non-customer-facing staging).
  - default_quant_profile: int8-dynamic
  - quant_fallback_policy: fall back to fp16 on mismatched kernels or if observed log-prob drop exceeds threshold configured per-model.

- Batching heuristics by archetype
  - Session-heavy chat:
    - batch_window_ms: 25ms
    - max_batch_size: 48
    - per-session hotpath: allow immediate dispatch for messages with user_ttl_remaining < 30s to avoid perceived lag
    - prefer prefix_cache hit paths to bypass decoding compute where applicable (return cached prefix embeddings + incremental decode)
  - Stateless short-completions:
    - batch_window_ms: 8ms
    - max_batch_size: 128
    - aggressive token-level batching enabled (token-tiling) to increase GPU utilization on short tokens
  - Bursty mixed:
    - adaptive_batch_window: start 5ms and auto-increase to 40ms under low utilization, capped by SLOs

Spreadsheet and measurements to run (columns for the cost sweep)

Create a simple sheet with columns: workload_name, model, hardware_type, seq_in, seq_out_avg, rps, percent_sessions, batch_window_ms, max_batch_size, quant_profile, cache_hit_rate_est, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec_per_gpu, est_cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, quality_delta_percent, notes.

Entrypoint experiment: run a set of sweeps across 3 models (7B, 13B, 70B) and two hardware tiers (A100-80GB, H100) for each archetype. Capture cost delta and quality delta at 10%, 50%, 100% traffic under the recommended defaults above.

Rollout plan and safety checks

1) Canary 1 (5–10% traffic): enable int8-dynamic + default batch windows; monitor p95 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, and eval-set quality metric. Rollback triggers: p95 increase > 30ms, quality drop > 1.5%.
2) Canary 2 (25% traffic): enable adaptive batching for bursty workloads and prefix cache eviction tuning; observe cache hit-rate trend and token-per-second metric.
3) Full rollout (100%): promote if primary KPIs (unit cost down, p95 within SLO) hold for 48h. Maintain a 24h automated rollback window for quantization-induced regressions.

Quick AB metrics to record

- Unit token cost USD (measured by accounting pipeline)
- p50/p95/p99 latency (API-level)
- GPU-token throughput (tokens/sec/GPU)
- Prefix cache hit-rate and eviction churn
- Quality regression signal: cohort-based BLEU/ROUGE on synthetic eval set + delta in human-rated correctness sample

Risk profile and mitigations

- Risk: silent quality regressions from aggressive quantization.
  - Mitigation: staged quantization with automatic evaluation gates; sample-level logging and human review on triggers.
- Risk: user-visible tail-latency spikes due to batching.
  - Mitigation: conservative batch_window defaults, per-route SLO overrides, immediate-unbundle path for low-ttl requests.
- Risk: cache poisoning (incorrect prefix reuse across tenants/contexts).
  - Mitigation: strict namespace scoping, user-bound cache keys, and sampling-based correctness checks.

Operational notes and follow-ups

- Instrumentation: add a lightweight batch diagnostic event emitted on each dispatch: {route, batch_size, batch_window_ms, quant_profile, cache_hit}. This can initially be a structured log picked up by Console dashboards. (See linked PR.)
- Spreadsheet link: populate the linked sheet with baseline numbers for three customer trials (internal IDs); include a tab for cost-normalized comparisons.
- Next steps: run internal dry-run on staging with production-like traffic for each archetype; capture the spreadsheet columns above and share results in the next Optimization sync (week of 2025-02-19).

Appendix: short worked example

Example: support-chat (session-heavy), model=13B, baseline: 200 req/s, avg seq_in=32 tokens, avg seq_out=120 tokens, current p95=190ms, current token-cost est= $35 per 1M tokens. Applying defaults (batch_window_ms=25, max_batch_size=48, int8-dynamic, session_cache_ttl=900) produced these projected deltas from simulator: p95 +12ms, tokens/sec/GPU +28%, est token-cost -> $25 per 1M tokens (-29%), eval-set quality delta -0.5%.

Notes to readers

This is intentionally compact and pragmatic. Please capture any experimental results in the linked sheet and flag regressions on INF-3124. If you want a more conservative variant (prioritizing latency over cost) I can produce one-pager alternate defaults for sensitive enterprise routes.
